# Expertise

::: {.position-line}

Quantitative methods, built for application. The details of our work are in our publications and notes.

:::

<div class="sh"><h2>Methods</h2></div>
<div class="mblock" id="statistics"><div class="xblock"><span class="n">01</span><h3>Statistics and econometrics</h3><p>Measuring, testing and monitoring risk models with clear statistical guarantees.</p><p class="more">We develop calibration tests that stay reliable when defaults are rare, tools for quantiles and extreme values, and continuous, anytime-valid monitoring methods that detect drift without piling up false alarms.</p></div><div class="anim-group"><div class="anim-switch" role="group"><button type="button" data-pane="jeffreys" aria-pressed="true">Jeffreys calibration test</button><button type="button" data-pane="eprocess" aria-pressed="false">Continuous monitoring</button></div><div class="anim-pane" data-pane="jeffreys"><div class="storm-anim" data-anim="jeffreys"></div></div><div class="anim-pane" data-pane="eprocess" hidden><div class="storm-anim" data-anim="eprocess"></div></div></div></div>
<div class="mblock" id="machine-learning"><div class="xblock"><span class="n">02</span><h3>Machine learning and artificial intelligence</h3><p>More flexible models, provided they stay explainable, robust and validatable.</p><p class="more">We evaluate recent approaches — foundation models for tabular data, new architectures — without presupposition, with one simple question: what do they bring to risk modelling? Explainability, fairness and robustness count as much as performance.</p></div>
<div class="storm-anim" data-anim="tfm"></div>
</div>
<div class="mblock" id="stress-testing"><div class="xblock"><span class="n">03</span><h3>Stress testing and scenarios</h3><p>Propagating scenarios through risk models, or starting from the breaking threshold to work back to the most plausible scenario.</p><p class="more">Our frameworks are modular: each block can be replaced by an already-validated internal model. The same set-up then delivers more information — the full distribution, the extremes, the breaking scenarios — at the same computational cost.</p></div><div class="anim-group"><div class="anim-switch" role="group"><button type="button" data-pane="rst" aria-pressed="true">Reverse stress test</button><button type="button" data-pane="credit" aria-pressed="false">Credit stress test</button></div><div class="anim-pane" data-pane="rst"><div class="storm-anim" data-anim="rst"></div></div><div class="anim-pane" data-pane="credit" hidden><div class="storm-anim" data-anim="credit"></div></div></div></div>

<div class="xblocks"><div class="xblock app" id="credit"><h3>Credit risk</h3><p>Developing, validating and monitoring credit models, and measuring how they behave under stress.</p></div><div class="xblock app" id="climate"><h3>Climate risks</h3><p>Bringing physical and transition risks into the assessment of financial risk.</p></div><div class="xblock app" id="geopolitical"><h3>Geopolitical and macro-financial risk</h3><p>Understanding how shocks spread to portfolios, and which ones could put them in difficulty.</p></div></div>
